title.narrative: BCSDN Regional Civil Society Development Hub 2023-27
BCSDN Regional Civil Society Development Hub 2023-27

description.narrative: BCSDN är ett nätverk med 13 civilsamhällesorganisationer (CSOs) i den vidare Balkan-regionen. BCSDN verkar för att stärka civilsamhället och att påverka europeiska och nationella policys och program för en bättre tillvaro för civilsamhället som i förlängningen syftar till att säkerställa fungerande och hållbara demokratier i regionen. Sida ger stöd till BCSDN's Hub, som är en del av det bredare BCSDN-nätverket som syftar till att öka samarbete och motståndskraft hos civilsamhällesorganisationer på västra Balkan (Albanien, Bosnien-Hercegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, Nordmakedonien, Serbien). Programmet arbetar mot tre huvudsakliga mål: effektivt evidensbaserat påverkansarbete, ökad förståelse för vikten av en möjliggörande miljö för civila samhället att verka samt starkare regionalt samarbete för civilsamhället. Programmet stödjer bland annat arbetet med att analysera och "mäta" utrymmet för det civila samhället att verka i regionen. Slutsatserna från dessa studier används i nätverkets påverkansarbete på nationell, regional och EU-nivå. Även om BCSDN Hub framför allt handlar om västra Balkan-regionen med ovan nämna länder, ingår Turkiet i viss mån genom regionalt utbyte och gemensamt påverkansarbete.

The Balkan Civil Society Development Network is a network of 13 civil society organizations from the wider Balkan region. Its mission is to empower civil society and influence European and national policies towards a more enabling environment for civil society development to ensure sustainable and functioning democracies in the Balkans. Sida supports the BCSDN Hub, which is a program within the wider BCSDN’s work. The Hub aims to enhance the cooperation and resilience of civil society organisations in the Western Balkans. More specifically, the Hub works within the current program towards three immediate outcomes: effective evidence-based advocacy for civic space, increased understanding of the enabling environment, and stronger regional cooperation for civic space. Among other things, the Hub supports the monitoring of the enabling environment for civil society in the Western Balkan countries and use the findings for advocacy at country, regional, and EU-levels. The BCSDN Hub focuses on the Western Balkan 6 countries to which most of the funds go, but Türkiye is participating in regional exchange and joint advocacy work.

Ultimate outcome/impact: Enhanced cooperation and resilience of CSOs in the Western Balkan countries that contribute to open civic space.
Intermediate outcomes Positive changes in standards and legislation affecting the Enabling Environment for Civil Society Increased common understanding and cooperation for promoting civic space.
Immediate outcomes: Evidence-based advocacy for promoting the enabling environment and civic space Improved awareness of key stakeholders about enabling environment standards and civic space state of play in the Western Balkans Strengthened CSO and multi-stakeholder collaboration for protecting the civic space.

Enabling environment monitored and findings recognised by stakeholders
The methodology for the monitoring matrix has been revised and is now a more robust and refined tool that includes new aspects such as online civic space, anti-monely laundering and countering finance of terrorism (AML/CFT), and the strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPPs). The revised methodology has led to an improved analysis by BCSDN and its partners in the published Monitoring Matrix reports on the enabling environment (six national and one regional report). Civil society partners from the region were engaged in the data collection and analysis process.
Findings from the Monitoring Matrix reports have been incorporated in reports by other actors, such as the civil society initiative European Civic Space Report, and in EU reports, such as EU Rule of Law reports from July 2024 for Albaina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia. BCSDN notes that this reinforces their role as a key contributor in shaping EU policies on civil society in the Western Balkans.
Joint adovocacy contributed to changes
BCSDN's research on SLAPPs, and the resultsing report, has enchanced the understanding, raised public awareness, and driven concrete advocacy efforts and regional collaboration among civil society organisations to combat SLAPPs in the Western Balkans. As an example, the advocacy by the network has contributed to the development of a proposed Law on Citizen's Initiative and Protection of Citizens and Activists in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in other words an anti-SLAPP directive.
Advocacy by BCSDN and its members was more aligned, which contributed to a better understanding among external stakeholders of issues related to enabling environment, and reinforced the importance of creating a more supportive environment for civil society in the region, as well as promoting the role of civil society within and for the accession process of the Western Balkans and Türkiye. As an example, Council of Europe increased its understanding of the issues of how AML/CFT regulations and practices risk impact civil society organisations negatively, and has committed to revise a report on the matter to prevent misinterpretation and ensure clarity. Another example is the European Economic and Social Committee's (EESC) launch of the initiative Enlargement Candidate Members, which aims at enabling formal representation of candidate countries' civil society representatives, including BCSDN representatives. This is something that BCSDN had advocated for during during several years. Another BCSDN advocacy aim was fulfilled with DG JUST announcing the inclusion of enlargement countries in the EC Annual Rule of Law reports, which rely on strong input from civil society.
BCSDNs regional advocacy raised awareness of critical country-related civic space challenges. By coordinating rapid responses and fostering regional solidarity, BCSDN addressed key threats, such as a SLAPP case in North Macedonia, and supported the citizens' uprising in Serbia against election irregularities. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, BCSDN took several actions to react and raise awareness on the draft "foregin agents" law. Among other things, BCSDN's effort contributed to that Bosnia and Herzogivina was added to the CIVICUS Monitors' Monitor watchlist, and that the UN Special Rapporteur on the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms expressed their concerns over the draft law, and requested its urgent withdrawal. In the end, the draft law was withdrawn from the Bosnian Serb Assembly. BCSDN believes that their and members' advocacy efforts and actions contributed to the withdrawal.
BCSDN designed a Rapid Alert Mechanism (RAM) to facilitate quick responses to attacks on civil society and threats to civic space by connecting CSOs, media, and the international community. This has resulted in faster information sharing, increased citizen awareness, and stronger advocacy efforts, pressuring policymakers and decision-makers to take necessary measures to protect civic space.
Strenthened CSO collaboration
The anti-SLAPP efforts by BCSDN have effectively strengthened regional cooperation and raised awareness of the growing threat to basic freedoms. By fostering collaboration among various stakeholders affected, these efforts have led to the development of strategic approaches of how the civil society can address SLAPPs.
Three working groups were established to respond to recent civic space challenges and enable regular information exchange and facilitate regional collaboration among BCSDN members and other relevant CSOs on pressing civic space challenges in the region.
